Operations are scheduled to take place 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from January 12, 2026, through December 31, 2026.

Wave Glider vehicles will be deployed in the vicinity of Moss Landing and will operate continuously between latitudes 36.30000° N and 37.20000° N, extending shoreward from as far west as -122.97650° W. Each Wave Glider is approximately 8 feet by 2 feet (surfboard size), yellow/copper in color, with a contact plaque and a mast extending 1 meter above the water surface supporting a flag. The vehicles are wave-powered, carry no fuel, lubricants, or hydrocarbon

d: The Dutra Group will conduct marine operations for levee breach closure and rehabilitation along Suisun Slough adjacent to Joice Island near Suisun City, California, at approximately 38.191301, -122.035389. Waterside work will begin on or about October 5, 2026, and continue through no later than November 30, 2026. Operations will include the Crane Barge TM20, work boat, tugboat, and rotating flat deck barges. The crane barge will be spudded at various locations within the construction area. Flat deck barges will transit between the project site and the San Rafael Rock Quarry and may be moored at pre-existing moorings along Suisun Slough during mobilization. Work will occur during daylight hours; however, barge movements outside the construction area may continue at all hours. The Dutra Group will conduct dredging operations at the San Joaquin River/Stockton Deep Water Ship Channel, at approximately 38.09858, -121.58630 (NOAA Chart 18660), from on or about October 9, 2026, through on or about November 30, 2026. Operations will be conducted 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Clamshell dredge DB 24 or Beaver will conduct dredging operations, with a fleet of three split-hull disposal scows with capacities of 2,000 and 3,000 cubic yards. Tow tug Sarah Reed, or similar, will support disposal operations to Roberts Island I and use call sign KX7468. Tender tug Becky T or Phyllis T will provide additional support. All equipment will monitor VHF-FM channels 13, 14, and 80A. For more information, contact Superintendent Dennis Salyers at (415) 497-5289. Curtin Maritime (CMC) will conduct maintenance dredging within the existing U.S. Coast Guard entrance channel and dock at Horseshoe Cove from on or about October 22, 2026, through on or about October 28, 2026. Operations will be conducted Monday through Friday from 0700 to 1700. Dredging will begin in the entrance channel adjacent to the jetty, progress northwest, and then proceed inbound to the U.S. Coast Guard dock. Mechanical dredging will be performed by DB Ironbound (150 feet by 54 feet by 9 feet), with material loaded into scows Arrow Point and Long Point, each with a 1,450-cubic-yard capacity, and transported to the Alcatraz Disposal Site, SF-11, at approximately 37.82167, -122.41112, or the Montezuma Wetlands Restoration Project Dock at approximately 38.07194, -121.85944.
